result.evidence: Word count is about 150, slightly over the ~147 cap, so c4 loses points. The paragraph is coherent and runs problem-method-findings in order, but the casual second person ("You lose a lot", "You will still need") is a stylistic issue. Fidelity defects (c1): "builds four new" channels is inaccurate, because PC is the existing baseline and only three channels are new. "The other models got that low in far fewer instances" is roughly right, since the body says not greater than 6%. "You will still need the diamond norm to get this working" overstates the body, which says the diamond norm is "more natural" for multi-qubit use, not that it is required. "Usually tested" is mild embellishment. Coverage gaps (c2): the channels PC/CC/PMC/CMC are not named, and the claim that adding Clifford and/or measurement errors always improves accuracy is missing. Amplitude damping results are also absent, as is the compact-distribution finding. Validity (c3): the fidelity condition is too vague; the abstract says "keeps the fidelity constraint" without stating that the approximation must have smaller fidelity than the target. It does not overclaim logical error-rate results.
